title: What If You Shrank to the Size of an Ant? You'd Go Blind First

scenes.text: What if you shrank to the size of an ant? The first thing you'd lose is your eyesight.
Your pupil would be smaller than ten wavelengths of light. Light bends around an opening that small, so everything turns into a fuzzy blur.
Your voice, modelled as tiny vibrating strings, jumps from about 200 hertz to about 3,500. A squeak nobody can hear.
Your own hearing cuts off below about 340 hertz. Normal human speech sits around 200. Your friends are silent.
Then you'd gasp. Engineers at Virginia Tech calculated that each tiny breath catches so few oxygen molecules, it feels like standing at 7,998 metres. Everest's death zone.
Blind, deaf, squeaking and gasping. And starving: per kilogram, your metabolism would run about a hundred times faster. Still want the suit?

description:
What if you shrank to the size of an ant? University of Minnesota physicist James Kakalios explains that your pupil would be smaller than ten wavelengths of light, so diffraction would blur everything; your voice would rise from about 200 Hz to about 3,500 Hz and your hearing would cut off below roughly 340 Hz, so normal speech would be inaudible.
Virginia Tech engineers Max Mikel-Stites and Anne Staples calculated for the American Physical Society that an insect-sized human would catch so few oxygen molecules per breath that it would feel like 7,998 metres of altitude, the edge of Everest's death zone, while metabolic rate per kilogram rises about a hundredfold.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The Virginia Tech team's fix was a helmet with microscopic air pumps, which is exactly what the movie superhero wears. How small would you dare to go? Drop your own what-if below.
